pitch-law.description: D-STAR pitch law: decoded pitch matches DVSI, quality improves, level and band balance hold, other modes untouched.

shelf.description: High-band shelf re-tuned toward DVSI: 2-4 kHz error to DVSI falls; level, low bands, clipping and quality hold.

tones.description: Tone frames match DVSI's decoder on steady windows; speech PCM is unchanged.

low-band.description: Low-frequency roll-off matched to DVSI's decoders: closer to DVSI's output, nothing else regresses.

encoder.description: D-STAR encoder changes: our encoding, decoded by this library, gets closer to the input without hurting pitch, voicing or level; the decoder is untouched.

encoder-level.description: D-STAR encoder level handling: our encoding keeps the input level as DVSI's encoder does (both decoded by this library) without hurting spectral fit, pitch or voicing; the decoder is untouched.

ambe2450-imbe-encoders.description: AMBE+2 and IMBE encoders: our encoding, decoded by this library, keeps DVSI's level, fits the input at least as well as DVSI's own encoding, stays on pitch and voices like DVSI, sends no tone frames for speech, and clips no more than a few samples where the input itself reaches the rails (t03, t04); the decoders and the D-STAR encoder are untouched (D-STAR's encoded bits identical, so the baseline must record encoder-row hashes).

ambe2450-encoder-tones.description: AMBE+2 encoder tone frames: the tone indices and levels DVSI's encoder sends for its tone vectors, and few tone frames where DVSI sends voice.

dstar-encoder-tones.description: D-STAR encoder tone frames: the tone indices and volumes DVSI's encoder sends for its D-STAR tone vectors, and few tone frames where DVSI sends voice (KNOX tones among them); the AMBE+2 encoder's tone frames and both decoders' tone output unchanged.

call-progress-timing.description: Call-progress tones sent once they fill three spans and held two frames after, as DVSI's encoders send them: no vector gets many tone frames where DVSI sends voice (the 40-45 ms bursts of cpvbad got 45 frames), agreement with DVSI's tone frames does not fall, levels hold, and both decoders' tone output is unchanged.

tone-edges.description: DTMF, KNOX and single tones sent for the frames whose span they fill at least 45% wherever they start within the detector's blocks, and where one changes directly to another, the frame holding both carrying the newer tone if it is a DTMF or KNOX tone filling the span's newest half, else the older if it fills the oldest half, as DVSI's encoders send them: agreement with DVSI's tone frames rises in both encoders, tone frames where DVSI sends voice stay rare, levels hold, and both decoders' tone output is unchanged.

dvsi-parity-development.description: DVSI parity (D-STAR absolute gain and shelf; rate-33 bit layout, pitch law and error counts; output high-pass phase; voiced and unvoiced render gains): our decode of DVSI's bits is no further from DVSI's decoder, the IMBE encoder's bits are unchanged, and the D-STAR and rate-33 encoders' output, decoded by one decoder, is no further from DVSI's encoding.

dvsi-parity-validation.description: DVSI parity (D-STAR absolute gain and shelf; rate-33 bit layout, pitch law and error counts; output high-pass phase; voiced and unvoiced render gains): our decode of DVSI's bits is no further from DVSI's decoder, the IMBE encoder's bits are unchanged, and the D-STAR and rate-33 encoders' output, decoded by one decoder, is no further from DVSI's encoding.

dvsi-parity-final.description: DVSI parity (D-STAR absolute gain and shelf; rate-33 bit layout, pitch law and error counts; output high-pass phase; voiced and unvoiced render gains): our decode of DVSI's bits is no further from DVSI's decoder, the IMBE encoder's bits are unchanged, and the D-STAR and rate-33 encoders' output, decoded by one decoder, is no further from DVSI's encoding.

dvsi-parity-tones.description: DVSI parity: no tone vector's tone output agrees less often with DVSI's decoder, plays a wrong tone more often, or has its encoder tone frames agree less often with DVSI's.

dvsi-parity-channel.description: DVSI parity under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors): at no error rate do our mute decisions agree less often with DVSI's, for hard or soft decisions, and on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes (at least a tenth of those DVSI plays) our hard-decision output is no further from DVSI's.

dstar-lost-frames.description: D-STAR b0 125..127 decode as lost frames and the encoder stops sending b0 124/125: DVSI's speech bits decode unchanged, and our encoding loses nothing against the input when both encodings are decoded by a decoder that plays b0 125 as voice (the decoder before this change), so both runs score the same frames.

dstar-repeat-limit-mute.description: D-STAR's repeat-limit mute fades out, keeps the prediction history and mutes at DVSI's level: DVSI's clean speech bits, which never reach the repeat limit, decode unchanged in every mode.

dstar-c0-uncorrectable-channel.description: D-STAR hard decisions play a frame with an uncorrectable C0 word as a lost frame that still predicts the next frame, and repeat no frame on its corrected-error count (#155): under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors) our D-STAR mute decisions agree no less often with DVSI's, for hard or soft decisions, and on the loud frames neither run nor DVSI mutes our D-STAR output is no further from DVSI's, for hard or soft decisions.

dstar-c0-uncorrectable-speech.description: The same change leaves DVSI's error-free speech bits decoding unchanged in every mode.

dstar-error-level-mute-channel.description: D-STAR hard decisions mute on an error level that counts parity bits and integrates slowly (0.99 level + corrected bits, above 342; #155): under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors) our D-STAR mute decisions agree no less often with DVSI's for hard or soft decisions; their mean over the four hard-decision vectors is at least 0.9975 (with the 1-5% vectors in full agreement, 0.99 at 10%); and on the loud frames neither run nor DVSI mutes our D-STAR output is on average no further from DVSI's, for hard or soft decisions, by more than 0.01 dB.

dstar-error-level-mute-speech.description: The same change leaves DVSI's error-free speech bits decoding unchanged in every mode.

dstar-tone-volume-fade-tones.description: A D-STAR tone that goes on at another volume moves to it over the first 80 samples before clipping (#155): on DVSI's tone vectors no steady-tone window of ours agrees less often with DVSI's, plays a wrong tone more often, or is further from DVSI's level, frequency or balance (the frames where the volume changes are scored outside the scoreboard).

dstar-tone-volume-fade-speech.description: The same change leaves DVSI's speech bits decoding unchanged in every mode.

voiced-amplitude-development.description: Voiced amplitude (every harmonic interpolated at steady pitch, its fourth root moving linearly, as on DVSI's AMBE-3000): in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits comes closer to DVSI's decoder by at least 0.1 dB of log-spectral distance, its envelope correlation with DVSI's and its distance from the input get no worse, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB, and the encoders' bits are unchanged.

voiced-amplitude-validation.description: Voiced amplitude (every harmonic interpolated at steady pitch, its fourth root moving linearly, as on DVSI's AMBE-3000): in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits comes closer to DVSI's decoder by at least 0.1 dB of log-spectral distance, its envelope correlation with DVSI's and its distance from the input get no worse, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB, and the encoders' bits are unchanged.

voiced-amplitude-final.description: Voiced amplitude (every harmonic interpolated at steady pitch, its fourth root moving linearly, as on DVSI's AMBE-3000): in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits comes closer to DVSI's decoder by at least 0.1 dB of log-spectral distance, its envelope correlation with DVSI's and its distance from the input get no worse, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB, and the encoders' bits are unchanged.

voiced-amplitude-channel.description: Voiced amplitude under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors): in every mode our mute decisions agree with DVSI's as often as before at every error rate, hard or soft, and on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes our hard-decision output is no further from DVSI's.

voiced-amplitude-tones.description: Voiced amplitude on the tone vectors: no D-STAR or rate-33 tone vector's tone output agrees less often with DVSI's decoder or plays a wrong tone more often.

noise-voicing-development.description: Voicing over background noise (#149): at low pitches, where noise passes the voicing test, a 500 Hz column holding little more than the learned background noise (steady mains hum included) is not voiced; magnitudes are unchanged. In every mode our encoding voices like DVSI's more often and voices fewer of DVSI's unvoiced frames, loses no voiced frames or bands (at most 1% of DVSI's voiced frames and 2% of its voiced 1 kHz bands on any vector; of its voiced frames below 80 Hz, 2% on average and 15% on any vector, which hold few), stays as close to DVSI's encoding in spectrum, envelope and level, keeps its pitch, clips no more on any vector, and the decoders are untouched.

noise-voicing-validation.description: Voicing over background noise (#149): at low pitches, where noise passes the voicing test, a 500 Hz column holding little more than the learned background noise (steady mains hum included) is not voiced; magnitudes are unchanged. In every mode our encoding voices like DVSI's more often and voices fewer of DVSI's unvoiced frames, loses no voiced frames or bands (at most 1% of DVSI's voiced frames and 2% of its voiced 1 kHz bands on any vector; of its voiced frames below 80 Hz, 2% on average and 15% on any vector, which hold few), stays as close to DVSI's encoding in spectrum, envelope and level, keeps its pitch, clips no more on any vector, and the decoders are untouched.

noise-voicing-final.description: Voicing over background noise (#149): at low pitches, where noise passes the voicing test, a 500 Hz column holding little more than the learned background noise (steady mains hum included) is not voiced; magnitudes are unchanged. In every mode our encoding voices like DVSI's more often and voices fewer of DVSI's unvoiced frames, loses no voiced frames or bands (at most 1% of DVSI's voiced frames and 2% of its voiced 1 kHz bands on any vector; of its voiced frames below 80 Hz, 2% on average and 15% on any vector, which hold few), stays as close to DVSI's encoding in spectrum, envelope and level, keeps its pitch, clips no more on any vector, and the decoders are untouched.

noise-voicing-tones.description: Voicing over background noise on DVSI's tone vectors: on no vector do the encoders' tone frames agree less often with DVSI's or add tone frames where DVSI sends voice.

voiced-phase-development.description: Voiced phase (DVSI's onset restart and pitch-switch timing) and rate-33 V/UV rendering, development vectors: in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits correlates with DVSI's decoder waveform by at least 0.3 more, comes no further from it in log-spectral distance or envelope correlation, no further from the input than 0.02 dB, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB; the D-STAR and IMBE encoders' bits are unchanged and the rate-33 encoder's decode is no further from DVSI's encoding.

voiced-phase-validation.description: Voiced phase (DVSI's onset restart and pitch-switch timing) and rate-33 V/UV rendering, validation vectors: in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits correlates with DVSI's decoder waveform by at least 0.3 more, comes no further from it in log-spectral distance or envelope correlation, no further from the input than 0.02 dB, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB; the D-STAR and IMBE encoders' bits are unchanged and the rate-33 encoder's decode is no further from DVSI's encoding.

voiced-phase-final.description: Voiced phase (DVSI's onset restart and pitch-switch timing) and rate-33 V/UV rendering, final vectors: in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits correlates with DVSI's decoder waveform by at least 0.3 more, comes no further from it in log-spectral distance or envelope correlation, no further from the input than 0.02 dB, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB; the D-STAR and IMBE encoders' bits are unchanged and the rate-33 encoder's decode is no further from DVSI's encoding.

voiced-phase-channel.description: Voiced phase under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors): in every mode our mute decisions agree with DVSI's as often as before at every error rate, hard or soft, and on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes our hard-decision output is no further from DVSI's.

voiced-phase-tones.description: Voiced phase on the tone vectors: no D-STAR or rate-33 tone vector's tone output agrees less often with DVSI's decoder or plays a wrong tone more often, and the encoders' tone frames agree with DVSI's as often as before.

amplitude-limit-development.description: Amplitude limit (no eq 116 scaling on the IMBE and rate-33 paths, as DVSI's decoders), development vectors: P25 and rate 33 come no further from DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance, envelope or waveform correlation and no further from the input than 0.02 dB, their level moves by at most 0.2 dB; D-STAR's PCM and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

amplitude-limit-validation.description: Amplitude limit (no eq 116 scaling on the IMBE and rate-33 paths, as DVSI's decoders), validation vectors: P25 and rate 33 come no further from DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance, envelope or waveform correlation and no further from the input than 0.02 dB, their level moves by at most 0.2 dB; D-STAR's PCM and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

amplitude-limit-channel.description: Amplitude limit under channel errors: in every mode mute decisions agree with DVSI's as often as before at every error rate, hard or soft, and on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes our hard-decision output is no further from DVSI's.

amplitude-limit-tones.description: Amplitude limit on the tone vectors: no D-STAR or rate-33 tone vector's tone output agrees less often with DVSI's decoder or plays a wrong tone more often.

unvoiced-subframes-development.description: Unvoiced synthesis as DVSI's decoders render it (DVSI's noise sequence, 10 ms subframes under square-root triangular windows, a mid-frame subframe between the two frames' models), development vectors: in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits comes at least 0.5 dB closer to DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance and no further on any vector, correlates with its waveform sample against sample at least 0.005 more, keeps its envelope correlation, comes no further from the input than 0.02 dB, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB, and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

unvoiced-subframes-validation.description: Unvoiced synthesis as DVSI's decoders render it (DVSI's noise sequence, 10 ms subframes under square-root triangular windows, a mid-frame subframe between the two frames' models), validation vectors: in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits comes at least 0.5 dB closer to DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance and no further on any vector, correlates with its waveform sample against sample at least 0.005 more, keeps its envelope correlation, comes no further from the input than 0.02 dB, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB, and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

unvoiced-subframes-final.description: Unvoiced synthesis as DVSI's decoders render it (DVSI's noise sequence, 10 ms subframes under square-root triangular windows, a mid-frame subframe between the two frames' models), final vectors: in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits comes at least 0.5 dB closer to DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance and no further on any vector, correlates with its waveform sample against sample at least 0.005 more, keeps its envelope correlation, comes no further from the input than 0.02 dB, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB, and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

unvoiced-subframes-channel.description: Unvoiced synthesis under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors): in every mode our mute decisions agree with DVSI's as often as before at every error rate, hard or soft, and on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes our hard-decision output is no further from DVSI's.

unvoiced-subframes-tones.description: Unvoiced synthesis on the tone vectors: no D-STAR or rate-33 tone vector's tone output agrees less often with DVSI's decoder or plays a wrong tone more often, and the encoders' tone frames agree with DVSI's as often as before.

voiced-subframes-development.description: Voiced synthesis as DVSI's decoders render it (two 10 ms subframes per frame, pitch pulses playing each model's response, and the frame marks that start and end voiced runs), development vectors: in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits correlates with DVSI's waveform sample against sample at least 0.03 more, comes no further from DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance and by at most 0.05 dB on any vector, keeps its envelope correlation, comes no further from the input than 0.02 dB, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB, and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

voiced-subframes-validation.description: Voiced synthesis as DVSI's decoders render it (two 10 ms subframes per frame, pitch pulses playing each model's response, and the frame marks that start and end voiced runs), validation vectors: in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits correlates with DVSI's waveform sample against sample at least 0.03 more, comes no further from DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance and by at most 0.05 dB on any vector, keeps its envelope correlation, comes no further from the input than 0.02 dB, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB, and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

voiced-subframes-final.description: Voiced synthesis as DVSI's decoders render it (two 10 ms subframes per frame, pitch pulses playing each model's response, and the frame marks that start and end voiced runs), final vectors: in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits correlates with DVSI's waveform sample against sample at least 0.03 more, comes no further from DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance and by at most 0.05 dB on any vector, keeps its envelope correlation, comes no further from the input than 0.02 dB, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB, and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

voiced-subframes-channel.description: Voiced synthesis in subframes under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors): in every mode our mute decisions agree with DVSI's as often as before at every error rate, hard or soft, and on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes our hard-decision output is no further from DVSI's.

voiced-subframes-tones.description: Voiced synthesis in subframes on the tone vectors: no D-STAR or rate-33 tone vector's tone output agrees less often with DVSI's decoder or plays a wrong tone more often, and the encoders' tone frames agree with DVSI's as often as before.

ambe2450-tone-fade-tones.description: Rate-33 tones crossfaded with the frames around them over 80 samples, as DVSI's decoder plays them: no rate-33 tone vector's tone level, frequency or twist moves further from DVSI's decoder, none agrees less often with its tone output or plays a wrong tone more often, and no D-STAR tone vector changes in any of these.

ambe2450-tone-fade-speech.description: Rate-33 tone crossfades: the speech vectors hold no tone frame, so every mode's decode of them is unchanged.

ambe2450-frames-development.description: Rate-33 frame handling as DVSI's decoder plays it (silence frames 13.8 dB lower on 15 bands, mutes that fade the last frame out under DVSI's noise level, the frame after a mute or a tone starting afresh, tone 255 and lost frames around tones), development vectors: no mode's decode of the speech vectors changes and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

ambe2450-frames-validation.description: Rate-33 frame handling as DVSI's decoder plays it (silence frames 13.8 dB lower on 15 bands, mutes that fade the last frame out under DVSI's noise level, the frame after a mute or a tone starting afresh, tone 255 and lost frames around tones), validation vectors: no mode's decode of the speech vectors changes and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

ambe2450-frames-final.description: Rate-33 frame handling as DVSI's decoder plays it (silence frames 13.8 dB lower on 15 bands, mutes that fade the last frame out under DVSI's noise level, the frame after a mute or a tone starting afresh, tone 255 and lost frames around tones), final vectors: no mode's decode of the speech vectors changes and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

ambe2450-frames-tones.description: Rate-33 frame handling on the tone vectors: no D-STAR tone vector changes in tone level, frequency, twist, detector agreement or wrong tones, and no rate-33 tone vector agrees less often with DVSI's decoder's tone output, plays a wrong tone more often, or moves its tone frequency or twist further from DVSI's, or its level by more than 0.05 dB.

ambe2450-frames-channel.description: Rate-33 frame handling under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors): in every mode our mute decisions agree with DVSI's no less often at any error rate, hard or soft, and on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes (at least a tenth of those DVSI plays) our hard-decision output is no further from DVSI's by more than 0.01 dB.

pcm-rounding-development.description: D-STAR and rate-33 16-bit output rounded to nearest, as DVSI's decoders round it, development vectors: P25's decode is unchanged; on no D-STAR or rate-33 vector does our decode come further from DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance by more than 0.01 dB or correlate with DVSI's waveform sample against sample less by more than 0.001, no vector's level moves by more than 0.05 dB, and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

pcm-rounding-validation.description: D-STAR and rate-33 16-bit output rounded to nearest, as DVSI's decoders round it, validation vectors: P25's decode is unchanged; on no D-STAR or rate-33 vector does our decode come further from DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance by more than 0.01 dB or correlate with DVSI's waveform sample against sample less by more than 0.001, no vector's level moves by more than 0.05 dB, and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

pcm-rounding-final.description: D-STAR and rate-33 16-bit output rounded to nearest, as DVSI's decoders round it, final vectors: P25's decode is unchanged; on no D-STAR or rate-33 vector does our decode come further from DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance by more than 0.01 dB or correlate with DVSI's waveform sample against sample less by more than 0.001, no vector's level moves by more than 0.05 dB, and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

pcm-rounding-tones.description: D-STAR and rate-33 16-bit output rounded to nearest, as DVSI's decoders round it, on the tone vectors: no D-STAR or rate-33 tone vector agrees less often with DVSI's decoder's tone output, plays a wrong tone more often, or moves its tone frequency or twist further from DVSI's, or its level by more than 0.05 dB.

pcm-rounding-channel.description: D-STAR and rate-33 16-bit output rounded to nearest, as DVSI's decoders round it, under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors): in every mode our mute decisions agree with DVSI's no less often at any error rate, hard or soft, and on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes (at least a tenth of those DVSI plays) our hard-decision output is no further from DVSI's by more than 0.01 dB.

unvoiced-code-development.description: A voice frame with no voiced band coded at one fixed pitch code per codec (D-STAR b0 123, rate 33 b0 119, P25 b0 127), its amplitudes measured on that code's harmonic grid, development vectors: every decode of DVSI's bits is unchanged, and for each encoder the log-spectral distance of its decoded encoding from DVSI's encoding and from the input rises by no more than 0.01 dB and its level gap to DVSI's encoding by no more than 0.1 dB.

unvoiced-code-validation.description: A voice frame with no voiced band coded at one fixed pitch code per codec (D-STAR b0 123, rate 33 b0 119, P25 b0 127), its amplitudes measured on that code's harmonic grid, validation vectors: every decode of DVSI's bits is unchanged, and for each encoder the log-spectral distance of its decoded encoding from DVSI's encoding and from the input rises by no more than 0.01 dB and its level gap to DVSI's encoding by no more than 0.1 dB.

unvoiced-code-tones.description: A voice frame with no voiced band coded at one fixed pitch code per codec, on the tone vectors: every decode of DVSI's bits is unchanged (no tone vector moves in detector agreement, wrong tones, tone level, frequency or twist in any mode), and on no D-STAR or rate-33 vector do the encoder's tone frames agree less often with DVSI's or appear where DVSI sends voice more often.

unvoiced-code-channel.description: A voice frame with no voiced band coded at one fixed pitch code per codec, under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors): every decode of DVSI's bits is unchanged, so in every mode the mute decisions agree with DVSI's exactly as before at every error rate, hard and soft, and the output on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes (at least a tenth of those DVSI plays) is as far from DVSI's as before.

joint-search-development.description: The D-STAR and AMBE+2 (rate-33) encoders refine their six spectral vector indices (b3..b8) together after the nearest-row search, two passes minimising the decoder's mean-removed residual error weighted by the square root of each harmonic's amplitude relative to the frame's geometric mean (bounded 0.1..10), and their magnitude scales are recalibrated, development vectors: every decode of DVSI's bits is unchanged, the IMBE encoder's bits are unchanged, and for the D-STAR and rate-33 encoders the log-spectral distance of the decoded encoding from DVSI's encoding and from the input rises by no more than 0.01 dB, its envelope correlation with the input falls by no more than 0.002, and its level gap to DVSI's encoding grows by no more than 0.1 dB.

joint-search-validation.description: The D-STAR and AMBE+2 (rate-33) encoders refine their six spectral vector indices (b3..b8) together after the nearest-row search, two passes minimising the decoder's mean-removed residual error weighted by the square root of each harmonic's amplitude relative to the frame's geometric mean (bounded 0.1..10), and their magnitude scales are recalibrated, validation vectors: every decode of DVSI's bits is unchanged, the IMBE encoder's bits are unchanged, and for the D-STAR and rate-33 encoders the log-spectral distance of the decoded encoding from DVSI's encoding and from the input rises by no more than 0.01 dB, its envelope correlation with the input falls by no more than 0.002, and its level gap to DVSI's encoding grows by no more than 0.1 dB.

joint-search-tones.description: The D-STAR and AMBE+2 (rate-33) encoders refine their six spectral vector indices (b3..b8) together after the nearest-row search, two passes minimising the decoder's mean-removed residual error weighted by the square root of each harmonic's amplitude relative to the frame's geometric mean (bounded 0.1..10), and their magnitude scales are recalibrated, on the tone vectors: every decode of DVSI's bits is unchanged (no tone vector moves in detector agreement, wrong tones, tone level, frequency or twist in any mode), and the D-STAR and rate-33 encoders' tone results are unchanged on every vector (agreement with DVSI's tone frames, tone frames where DVSI sends voice, and the level of the tone frames both send).

joint-search-channel.description: The D-STAR and AMBE+2 (rate-33) encoders refine their six spectral vector indices (b3..b8) together after the nearest-row search, two passes minimising the decoder's mean-removed residual error weighted by the square root of each harmonic's amplitude relative to the frame's geometric mean (bounded 0.1..10), and their magnitude scales are recalibrated, under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors): every decode of DVSI's bits is unchanged, so in every mode the mute decisions agree with DVSI's exactly as before at every error rate, hard and soft, and the output on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes (at least a tenth of those DVSI plays) is as far from DVSI's as before.

r33-row-grid-development.description: Rate-33 voice frames of V/UV rows 18 to 31 decode on a band grid whose L bands span 3.58 kHz (w0 = 2.81 / L, L from the pitch code, the unvoiced factor from that w0), as the published AMBE-3000R measurement gives and DVSI's decoder plays them, development vectors: the D-STAR and P25 decodes of DVSI's bits are unchanged, every encoder's bits are unchanged, and for rate 33 the log-spectral distance from DVSI's decode falls (mean, 95% interval below 0), the sample-for-sample waveform correlation and the envelope correlation with DVSI's decode fall by no more than 0.0005, the level against DVSI's moves by at most 0.05 dB (mean and every vector), and the log-spectral distance from the input rises by no more than 0.005 dB.

r33-row-grid-validation.description: Rate-33 voice frames of V/UV rows 18 to 31 decode on a band grid whose L bands span 3.58 kHz (w0 = 2.81 / L, L from the pitch code, the unvoiced factor from that w0), as the published AMBE-3000R measurement gives and DVSI's decoder plays them, validation vectors: the D-STAR and P25 decodes of DVSI's bits are unchanged, every encoder's bits are unchanged, and for rate 33 the log-spectral distance from DVSI's decode falls (mean, 95% interval below 0), the sample-for-sample waveform correlation and the envelope correlation with DVSI's decode fall by no more than 0.0005, the level against DVSI's moves by at most 0.05 dB (mean and every vector), and the log-spectral distance from the input rises by no more than 0.005 dB.

r33-row-grid-tones.description: Rate-33 voice frames of V/UV rows 18 to 31 decode on a band grid whose L bands span 3.58 kHz (w0 = 2.81 / L, L from the pitch code, the unvoiced factor from that w0), as the published AMBE-3000R measurement gives and DVSI's decoder plays them, on the tone vectors: the D-STAR and P25 decodes of DVSI's bits are unchanged, the D-STAR and rate-33 encoders' tone results are unchanged on every vector, and on no rate-33 vector does our decode agree less often with DVSI's tone output or play a wrong tone more often, or move its tone level or twist further from DVSI's by more than 0.01 dB or its tone frequency by more than 1e-4 relative. Tone frames decode as before; only a speech frame of these rows played under a tone's 80-sample fade-in can move a tone metric, by far less than these tolerances.

r33-row-grid-channel.description: Rate-33 voice frames of V/UV rows 18 to 31 decode on a band grid whose L bands span 3.58 kHz (w0 = 2.81 / L, L from the pitch code, the unvoiced factor from that w0), as the published AMBE-3000R measurement gives and DVSI's decoder plays them, under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors): the D-STAR and P25 decodes are unchanged (mute decisions and output on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes, hard and soft), and for rate 33 the mute decisions agree with DVSI's no less often on any vector, hard or soft, and the output on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes (at least a tenth of those DVSI plays) comes no further from DVSI's, hard or soft.

encoder-quality-final.description: The three changes of this change set together (the encoders' fixed pitch code for frames with no voiced band, the AMBE encoders' joint choice of their six spectral vectors with recalibrated magnitude scales, and rate-33 V/UV rows 18 to 31 on the published band grid), main against the change set, final vectors. Built from the development and validation gate sets of the three changes (unvoiced-code-*, joint-search-*, r33-row-grid-*) with the same metrics and rules: where two changes bound the same metric their limits are added, and 'unchanged' is kept only where it holds for the change set as a whole. r33-pulsed-rows-development.description: Rate 33's pulsed rows: this change set is to play AMBE 3600x2450's V/UV rows 18 to 31, which TIA-102.BABA-1 Annex B decodes as no band voiced and the library plays on the band grid as noise, as rate 33's form of the pulsed voicing state, in the rate-33 rendering only. A voice frame decoded with one of those rows whose model, as the synthesis renders it (after adaptive smoothing), has no voiced band is to be a pulsed-row frame with its row and its pitch code b0 (0..119); one whose smoothing voiced a harmonic renders as before. The row names the pulsed 500 Hz channels (channel k from 500 k to 500 (k + 1) Hz, the last open above 3500 Hz, lowest first) of the frame's own subframe and of its mid-frame subframe: rows 18 to 23 the own subframe only (18 channel 0, 19 channels 0-1, 20 all, 21 channel 2, 22 channel 7, 23 channels 5-7), rows 24 and 25 both (24 all in both, 25 channels 2-7 in both), rows 26 to 31 the mid-frame subframe only (26 channel 0, 27 channel 2, 28 all, 29 channels 0-1, 30 channel 7, 31 channels 6-7). In a model with no voiced band an unvoiced harmonic at f Hz is pulsed when the channel of f or of f + 250 Hz is pulsed in the mask that applies (the row's mid-frame mask for the mid-frame model, its own mask for the frame's own model and, through the stream's subframe state, for the next frame's first model), plays no noise and takes its magnitude with the unvoiced factor 0.2046 / sqrt(w0) taken out, as the pulsed state of the branch below does. A model with a pulsed band emits exactly one pulse, its model's point being sample 80 (mid-frame model) or 160 (own model) of the frame: for rows 18 to 23 and 26 to 31 at point + 1.016 b0 - 80.89 samples; for rows 24 and 25, whose code holds two positions on a grid of 11, the mid-frame model's at 80 - 75.6 + 11.875 (b0 mod 11) and the own model's at 160 - 75.6 + 11.875 (b0 div 11). The pulse is played by its own model only, as the voiced pulse response (the response window with that model's period, the voiced render gain, the regenerated phases the model carries) through that model's pulsed bands under that model's crossfade weight, rising in the interval that ends at its point and falling in the one that starts there, from the pulse's time (or the start of its model's window) until its response or its model's window ends: no alternation between neighbouring models and no pulse shared between two models, which is where rate 33 is to differ from P25 and D-STAR. The part of an own-model pulse that falls in the next frame is played there by the last frame's own model, which takes its pulsed bands and its pulse again from the row and code the frame stores in the stream's subframe state. The voiced pulse train, the mid-frame voicing and the mid-frame pitch are to stay as they are (a model with pulsed bands counts as one with no voiced band); a silence frame's mid-frame model takes no pulsed band; a frame starting from silence plays nothing of the last frame's own model. A lost frame's repeat (and the repeat under a tone's first frame) is to play the repeated model's own mask in both halves, each of its two models emitting its pulse at the own pulse's position relative to its point (rows 18 to 23 point + 1.016 b0 - 80.89, rows 24 and 25 point - 75.6 + 11.875 (b0 div 11)); a repeat of rows 26 to 31 has no pulsed band. D-STAR, P25, ProVoice, the TIA-102.BABA rendering of mbe_synthesizeSpeechf() and every encoder are to stay as they are, and so is rate 33 on any stream that holds no frame of rows 18 to 31. How it was found: on DVSI's rate-33 decodes of the 20 development and 5 validation vectors, by a scratch build of the library (a worktree at 47d8cf3 with environment switches, outside the repository). The fourteen pairs of masks were measured on those decodes (each pair equals one entry of the 56 patterns that the branch below takes from Table 2 of US 7,970,606, an observation made afterwards and not their source); the pulse times, the two-position code of rows 24 and 25 and their constants were fitted on them; the repeat rule rests on six lost frames of the hard-decision channel-error vectors (dam_e5_hd and dam_e10_hd), which is what was observed there and not an established property of DVSI's decoder. That scratch build was measured on the development, validation, tone, channel (hard and soft decisions) and rate-33 DTX vectors before this set was declared, with the scoreboard's own measures for rate 33 too (the scratch build against the tools of the branch below, both at their joint lags, encoders not run): development vs_dvsi.waveform_corr_unshifted +0.000778 (interval 0.000300 to 0.001396; smallest change +0.0000073), validation +0.001452 (0.000473 to 0.002828; smallest +0.000090); vs_dvsi.lsd_db -0.0545 (every vector falling, the least by 0.0036) and -0.0764 (the least by 0.0309); vs_dvsi.env_corr +0.00494 and +0.00331; ours.lsd_db, the distance from the input speech, +0.0080 (largest ucarm20a +0.0253) and +0.0163 (largest t04 +0.0357); vs_dvsi.level_offset_db -0.0033 and -0.0065; on the tone partition the five tone metrics unchanged (tone.detector_agreement +0.00006 in the mean, no vector down); on the channel partition the eight mute metrics identical, channel.hd.lsd_common_db -0.0122 (coverage 0.750) and channel.sd.lsd_common_db -0.0123 (coverage 0.991). So none of those partitions is out of sample for the rule, and the limits below were set knowing those figures; no build was measured on the held-out partition (irstia and mark). The distance from the input speech rising is the change's measured cost, which these checks allow within their limits and do not hide. The baseline is the head of the branch below, fix/pulsed-state (2b6b6c2). The baseline against the change, development vectors (in sample: the rule was found on them). The max 0 checks say that no D-STAR or P25 decode of the run's speech vectors changes (their PCM hashes, the development and validation vectors of the run together; a hash missing on either side counts as a change) and that no encoder row of the run's speech vectors changes in any mode (their row hashes; this counter skips a vector whose baseline holds no row hash, so 'no encoder row changes' rests on every speech vector carrying a row hash in both runs, which is to be counted in both reports and stated with the result); they say nothing of other inputs or of which frames moved. For rate 33, decoding DVSI's bits: the increase rule asks for a mean gain in waveform correlation with DVSI's decode, sample against sample at lag 0, of at least 0.0005 with its bootstrap 95% interval (resampling whole recordings) above 0, and the decrease rule a mean fall in log-spectral distance from DVSI's decode of at least 0.03 dB with its interval below 0; all_no_decrease 0.0001 allows no vector's correlation to fall by more than 0.0001, and all_no_increase 0.005 no vector's distance from DVSI's decode to rise by more than 0.005 dB; the envelope correlation with DVSI's decode may fall by no more than 0.0005 in the mean, the distance from the input speech (ours.lsd_db) rise by no more than 0.02 dB in the mean, and the level against DVSI's move by no more than 0.05 dB in the mean. Every paired check requires a measurement on every vector of the partition (every_vector), which makes a check need the figure everywhere and does not turn a limit on the mean into one on each vector: ours.lsd_db bounds the mean cost against the input speech and does not bound any one vector's, and the envelope and level checks likewise limit no single vector. The measures are the scoreboard's, on the frames it measures; they do not say which frames moved, nor how the change sounds against the input beyond the log-spectral distance. Coverage, read on the baseline's own scoreboard of the development, validation, tone and channel partitions (a build of git archive 2b6b6c2 scoring itself, aligned freely) before this set was declared: every paired metric checked here is measured in rate 33 on all 20 vectors of the partition, and all 20 vectors carry a speech PCM hash and an encoder-row hash in each mode.

The row names the pulsed 500 Hz channels (channel k from 500 k to 500 (k + 1) Hz, the last open above 3500 Hz, lowest first) of the frame's own subframe and of its mid-frame subframe: rows 18 to 23 the own subframe only (18 channel 0, 19 channels 0-1, 20 all, 21 channel 2, 22 channel 7, 23 channels 5-7), rows 24 and 25 both (24 all in both, 25 channels 2-7 in both), rows 26 to 31 the mid-frame subframe only (26 channel 0, 27 channel 2, 28 all, 29 channels 0-1, 30 channel 7, 31 channels 6-7). In a model with no voiced band an unvoiced harmonic at f Hz is pulsed when the channel of f or of f + 250 Hz is pulsed in the mask that applies (the row's mid-frame mask for the mid-frame model, its own mask for the frame's own model and, through the stream's subframe state, for the next frame's first model), plays no noise and takes its magnitude with the unvoiced factor 0.2046 / sqrt(w0) taken out, as the pulsed state of the branch below does. A model with a pulsed band emits exactly one pulse, its model's point being sample 80 (mid-frame model) or 160 (own model) of the frame: for rows 18 to 23 and 26 to 31 at point + 1.016 b0 - 80.89 samples; for rows 24 and 25, whose code holds two positions on a grid of 11, the mid-frame model's at 80 - 75.6 + 11.875 (b0 mod 11) and the own model's at 160 - 75.6 + 11.875 (b0 div 11). The pulse is played by its own model only, as the voiced pulse response (the response window with that model's period, the voiced render gain, the regenerated phases the model carries) through that model's pulsed bands under that model's crossfade weight, rising in the interval that ends at its point and falling in the one that starts there, from the pulse's time (or the start of its model's window) until its response or its model's window ends: no alternation between neighbouring models and no pulse shared between two models, which is where rate 33 is to differ from P25 and D-STAR. The part of an own-model pulse that falls in the next frame is played there by the last frame's own model, which takes its pulsed bands and its pulse again from the row and code the frame stores in the stream's subframe state. The voiced pulse train, the mid-frame voicing and the mid-frame pitch are to stay as they are (a model with pulsed bands counts as one with no voiced band); a silence frame's mid-frame model takes no pulsed band; a frame starting from silence plays nothing of the last frame's own model. A lost frame's repeat (and the repeat under a tone's first frame) is to play the repeated model's own mask in both halves, each of its two models emitting its pulse at the own pulse's position relative to its point (rows 18 to 23 point + 1.016 b0 - 80.89, rows 24 and 25 point - 75.6 + 11.875 (b0 div 11)); a repeat of rows 26 to 31 has no pulsed band. D-STAR, P25, ProVoice, the TIA-102.BABA rendering of mbe_synthesizeSpeechf() and every encoder are to stay as they are, and so is rate 33 on any stream that holds no frame of rows 18 to 31. How it was found: on DVSI's rate-33 decodes of the 20 development and 5 validation vectors, by a scratch build of the library (a worktree at 47d8cf3 with environment switches, outside the repository). The fourteen pairs of masks were measured on those decodes (each pair equals one entry of the 56 patterns that the branch below takes from Table 2 of US 7,970,606, an observation made afterwards and not their source); the pulse times, the two-position code of rows 24 and 25 and their constants were fitted on them; the repeat rule rests on six lost frames of the hard-decision channel-error vectors (dam_e5_hd and dam_e10_hd), which is what was observed there and not an established property of DVSI's decoder. That scratch build was measured on the development, validation, tone, channel (hard and soft decisions) and rate-33 DTX vectors before this set was declared, with the scoreboard's own measures for rate 33 too (the scratch build against the tools of the branch below, both at their joint lags, encoders not run): development vs_dvsi.waveform_corr_unshifted +0.000778 (interval 0.000300 to 0.001396; smallest change +0.0000073), validation +0.001452 (0.000473 to 0.002828; smallest +0.000090); vs_dvsi.lsd_db -0.0545 (every vector falling, the least by 0.0036) and -0.0764 (the least by 0.0309); vs_dvsi.env_corr +0.00494 and +0.00331; ours.lsd_db, the distance from the input speech, +0.0080 (largest ucarm20a +0.0253) and +0.0163 (largest t04 +0.0357); vs_dvsi.level_offset_db -0.0033 and -0.0065; on the tone partition the five tone metrics unchanged (tone.detector_agreement +0.00006 in the mean, no vector down); on the channel partition the eight mute metrics identical, channel.hd.lsd_common_db -0.0122 (coverage 0.750) and channel.sd.lsd_common_db -0.0123 (coverage 0.991). So none of those partitions is out of sample for the rule, and the limits below were set knowing those figures; no build was measured on the held-out partition (irstia and mark). The distance from the input speech rising is the change's measured cost, which these checks allow within their limits and do not hide. The baseline is the head of the branch below, fix/pulsed-state (2b6b6c2). The baseline against the change, tone vectors. On the tone vectors: the max 0 checks say that no D-STAR or P25 decode changes, the speech vectors' (in a combined run) as well as the tone vectors' (their PCM hashes); the D-STAR and rate-33 encoders' tone frames agree with DVSI's, appear where DVSI sends voice and differ in level from DVSI's where both send a tone exactly as before on every vector that has the figure (abs_delta_max 0 with worst 0; the tones group holds no encoder-row hashes, so the encoders are compared here through their tone frames, not bit for bit); and for rate 33 the steady tones' frequency error against DVSI's output rises by no more than 0.0005 on any vector that has the figure, the tone level and the balance of a dual tone's two components move further from DVSI's by no more than 0.02 dB in the mean, the share of windows playing a wrong tone rises on no vector that has the figure, and the detector's agreement with DVSI's tone output falls by no more than 0.005 on any vector. Coverage, read on the baseline's own scoreboard of the four partitions (a build of git archive 2b6b6c2 scoring itself) before this set was declared: rate 33's detector agreement and the D-STAR and rate-33 encoders' extra-tone rates are measured on all 52 tone vectors, so those checks require every vector; in rate 33 the frequency, level and wrong-tone figures are measured on all but cp1, cpvbad and dtmfvbad, and the balance on all but those three and alert; D-STAR's encoder agreement and volume error on all but cpvbad and the 16 KNOX vectors; the rate-33 encoder's agreement and level error on all but cpvbad; and all 52 tone vectors carry a PCM hash in each mode. A check on a metric that applies to part of the partition cannot require every vector, so a vector that lost the figure in both runs would pass it unnoticed. What the checks do not establish: the tone measures are an acoustic detector's, on the windows it calls steady in DVSI's output, and cover the scoreboard's steady tone windows, not the voice frames between and around the tones, which is where this change acts in these vectors; the scoreboard does not compare tone frames sample for sample; the level and balance checks are on means and limit no single vector.

low-band-development.description: DVSI's low band: this change set is to render the low band of the three decoders measured against DVSI's AMBE-3000 (D-STAR, P25 and AMBE 3600x2450 rate 33: their subframe renderings and their unvoiced synthesis) in two parts. A fixed part: a third-order Butterworth high-pass at 75 Hz, in magnitude and in phase (gain x^3 / sqrt(1 + x^6), phase the argument of s^3 / ((s + 1)(s^2 + s + 1)) at s = j x, x = f / 75 Hz), in place of the second-order Butterworth high-pass at 100 Hz the library renders there now (the phase at which the D-STAR and rate-33 tones start follows the fixed filter: which of the two filters it is to take is left to the tone measures to decide). And an adaptive low cut: a tracker T, 110 Hz at the start of a stream, follows the fundamental f0 of the frames whose model, as the synthesis renders it (after adaptive smoothing), has every band voiced (speech only: a positive pitch, no tone model), T <- T + 0.043 (f0 - T), and stands still through every other frame; the corner a frame applies is min(T, 200 Hz), the ceiling clipping the corner and not the tracker; a voiced harmonic at a frequency f under the corner is scaled by (f / corner)^2, its phase untouched, and one at or above the corner is not scaled at all; and the bins of the unvoiced transform whose centre frequency lies under the corner are zero, after each band has been scaled against its own noise power, the bins above keeping the level they had, the noise generator running as before. The tracker is stream state, kept in the caller-owned stream state beside the subframe rendering's pulse train and read only in a state that rendering wrote, any value no frame stores reading as a fresh stream's. The cut and the filter are properties of the rendering: the decoded models, their regenerated phases, the stored state and everything the encoders read keep the amplitudes as decoded. ProVoice (which has no DVSI material: it keeps the second-order filter at 100 Hz and no cut), the TIA-102.BABA rendering of mbe_synthesizeSpeechf() and every encoder are to stay byte for byte as they are, and no decoder's parameters, pitch law, mid-frame rule, pulsed state or gain change. How it was found: on DVSI's decodes of the 20 development and 5 validation vectors and of DVSI's 13 synthetic pulse-train vectors (ptrain0 to ptrain12, which the scoreboard scores in no partition), by a scratch build of the library (a worktree at 47d8cf3 with environment switches, outside the repository): DVSI's lowest harmonic, read frame by frame against ours, is a scaled copy of ours whose deficit is decoder state rather than a property of the frame (the same frames differ between recordings of the same speech), follows the pitch of the fully voiced frames only, and is a function of frequency, not of the harmonic's number; the tracker is the simplest rule found to fit, and its rate, ceiling and starting value, the power of the law and the fixed filter's corner and order are fits to those decodes, not values from a document; what DVSI's decoders compute is not known. That scratch build was measured on the development, validation, tone, channel and pulse-train vectors before this set was declared, with the scoreboard's own measures too, so none of those partitions is out of sample for the rule, and the limits below were set knowing those results; no build of this change was measured on the held-out partition (irstia and mark). The baseline is the head of the branch below, fix/ambe2450-pulsed-rows (9a101f8). The baseline against the change, development vectors (in sample: the rule was found on them). The max 0 check on encoder.rows_changed_vectors says that no encoder row of the run's speech vectors changes in any mode (the hashes of the bits each encoder emits; this counter skips a vector whose baseline holds no row hash, so 'no encoder row changes' rests on every speech vector carrying a row hash in both runs, which is to be counted in both reports and stated with the result): the encoders' bits must not change at all. The scoreboard's other encoder measures compare the two runs' encodings decoded by the candidate's decoder and are not checked here. It says nothing of other inputs. For each of the three codecs, decoding DVSI's bits: the increase rule asks for a mean gain in waveform correlation with DVSI's decode, sample against sample at lag 0 (vs_dvsi.waveform_corr_unshifted), of at least 0.0005 (D-STAR), 0.0007 (P25) and 0.0002 (rate 33) with its bootstrap 95% interval (resampling whole recordings) above 0; all_no_decrease allows no vector's correlation to fall by more than 0.0003 (D-STAR), 0.0001 (P25) and 0.0005 (rate 33), since in high voices, where the cut does nothing and only the fixed filter changes, single vectors may fall a little; the decrease rule asks for a mean fall in log-spectral distance from DVSI's decode (vs_dvsi.lsd_db) of at least 0.02 dB with its interval below 0, and all_no_increase 0.03 allows no vector's distance from DVSI's decode to rise by more than 0.03 dB; the envelope correlation with DVSI's decode may fall by no more than 0.0002 in the mean; the log-spectral distance from the input speech (ours.lsd_db) may rise by no more than 0.05 dB in the mean, which is the change's cost and is allowed, not hidden: DVSI's decoders remove fundamentals the input speech has, and a decode that follows them moves away from the input; the level against DVSI's decode (vs_dvsi.level_offset_db) may move by no more than 0.08 dB in the mean and 0.25 dB on any vector (the worst vector's change bounds every vector). Every paired check requires a measurement on every vector of the partition (every_vector), which makes a check need the figure everywhere and does not turn a limit on the mean into one on each vector: ours.lsd_db and the envelope correlation bound the mean and no single vector. The measures are the scoreboard's, on the frames it measures; they do not say which frames moved, whether the frames that move the tracker are those that move DVSI's, nor how the change sounds against the input beyond the log-spectral distance. Coverage, read on the baseline's own scoreboard of the development, validation, tone and channel partitions (a build of git archive 9a101f8 scoring itself, aligned freely) before this set was declared: every paired metric checked here is measured in each of the three modes on all 20 vectors of the partition, and all 20 vectors carry an encoder-row hash in each mode.

And an adaptive low cut: a tracker T, 110 Hz at the start of a stream, follows the fundamental f0 of the frames whose model, as the synthesis renders it (after adaptive smoothing), has every band voiced (speech only: a positive pitch, no tone model), T <- T + 0.043 (f0 - T), and stands still through every other frame; the corner a frame applies is min(T, 200 Hz), the ceiling clipping the corner and not the tracker; a voiced harmonic at a frequency f under the corner is scaled by (f / corner)^2, its phase untouched, and one at or above the corner is not scaled at all; and the bins of the unvoiced transform whose centre frequency lies under the corner are zero, after each band has been scaled against its own noise power, the bins above keeping the level they had, the noise generator running as before. The tracker is stream state, kept in the caller-owned stream state beside the subframe rendering's pulse train and read only in a state that rendering wrote, any value no frame stores reading as a fresh stream's. The cut and the filter are properties of the rendering: the decoded models, their regenerated phases, the stored state and everything the encoders read keep the amplitudes as decoded. ProVoice (which has no DVSI material: it keeps the second-order filter at 100 Hz and no cut), the TIA-102.BABA rendering of mbe_synthesizeSpeechf() and every encoder are to stay byte for byte as they are, and no decoder's parameters, pitch law, mid-frame rule, pulsed state or gain change. How it was found: on DVSI's decodes of the 20 development and 5 validation vectors and of DVSI's 13 synthetic pulse-train vectors (ptrain0 to ptrain12, which the scoreboard scores in no partition), by a scratch build of the library (a worktree at 47d8cf3 with environment switches, outside the repository): DVSI's lowest harmonic, read frame by frame against ours, is a scaled copy of ours whose deficit is decoder state rather than a property of the frame (the same frames differ between recordings of the same speech), follows the pitch of the fully voiced frames only, and is a function of frequency, not of the harmonic's number; the tracker is the simplest rule found to fit, and its rate, ceiling and starting value, the power of the law and the fixed filter's corner and order are fits to those decodes, not values from a document; what DVSI's decoders compute is not known. That scratch build was measured on the development, validation, tone, channel and pulse-train vectors before this set was declared, with the scoreboard's own measures too, so none of those partitions is out of sample for the rule, and the limits below were set knowing those results; no build of this change was measured on the held-out partition (irstia and mark). The baseline is the head of the branch below, fix/ambe2450-pulsed-rows (9a101f8). The baseline against the change, validation vectors (in sample: the rule was found on them). The max 0 check on encoder.rows_changed_vectors says that no encoder row of the run's speech vectors changes in any mode (the hashes of the bits each encoder emits; this counter skips a vector whose baseline holds no row hash, so 'no encoder row changes' rests on every speech vector carrying a row hash in both runs, which is to be counted in both reports and stated with the result): the encoders' bits must not change at all. The scoreboard's other encoder measures compare the two runs' encodings decoded by the candidate's decoder and are not checked here. It says nothing of other inputs. For each of the three codecs, decoding DVSI's bits: the increase rule asks for a mean gain in waveform correlation with DVSI's decode, sample against sample at lag 0 (vs_dvsi.waveform_corr_unshifted), of at least 0.0007 (D-STAR), 0.0007 (P25) and 0.0004 (rate 33) with its bootstrap 95% interval (resampling whole recordings) above 0; all_no_decrease allows no vector's correlation to fall by more than 0.0003 (D-STAR), 0.0001 (P25) and 0.0005 (rate 33), since in high voices, where the cut does nothing and only the fixed filter changes, single vectors may fall a little; the decrease rule asks for a mean fall in log-spectral distance from DVSI's decode (vs_dvsi.lsd_db) of at least 0.02 dB with its interval below 0, and all_no_increase 0.03 allows no vector's distance from DVSI's decode to rise by more than 0.03 dB; the envelope correlation with DVSI's decode may fall by no more than 0.0002 in the mean; the log-spectral distance from the input speech (ours.lsd_db) may rise by no more than 0.05 dB in the mean, which is the change's cost and is allowed, not hidden: DVSI's decoders remove fundamentals the input speech has, and a decode that follows them moves away from the input; the level against DVSI's decode (vs_dvsi.level_offset_db) may move by no more than 0.1 dB in the mean and 0.25 dB on any vector (the worst vector's change bounds every vector). Every paired check requires a measurement on every vector of the partition (every_vector), which makes a check need the figure everywhere and does not turn a limit on the mean into one on each vector: ours.lsd_db and the envelope correlation bound the mean and no single vector. The measures are the scoreboard's, on the frames it measures; they do not say which frames moved, whether the frames that move the tracker are those that move DVSI's, nor how the change sounds against the input beyond the log-spectral distance. Coverage, read on the baseline's own scoreboard of the development, validation, tone and channel partitions (a build of git archive 9a101f8 scoring itself, aligned freely) before this set was declared: every paired metric checked here is measured in each of the three modes on all 5 vectors of the partition, and all 5 vectors carry an encoder-row hash in each mode.

block-lengths-development.description: The AMBE block lengths at 20 harmonics: this change set is to code the log-magnitude prediction residual of a frame of 20 harmonics in blocks of 4, 5, 5 and 6 harmonics, in place of the 4, 4, 6 and 6 that Annex C of TIA-102.BABA-1 prints for L = 20, in both AMBE decoders and both AMBE encoders measured against DVSI's AMBE-3000 (D-STAR and AMBE 3600x2450 rate 33), decoder and encoder alike. Nothing else is to change: no other row of the table, no codebook, pitch law, gain table or synthesis rule; P25 (IMBE decoding and the IMBE encoder), ProVoice, TETRA and the TIA-102.BABA rendering of mbe_synthesizeSpeechf() are to stay byte for byte as they are, and so are both AMBE decoders and both AMBE encoders on every stream that holds no frame of 20 harmonics. How it was found: on DVSI's decodes of the 20 development and 5 validation vectors, by a scratch build of the library (a worktree at 47d8cf3 with environment switches, outside the repository): the spectral shape error of the strong harmonics, split by the frame's harmonic count, stands out at 20 harmonics in D-STAR and rate 33 alike and nowhere else, and with the blocks 4, 5, 5, 6 it falls to the level of the other counts, as no other division tried does; and the decode of DVSI's own encodings with that division comes as near the input speech those encodings were made from as at the neighbouring counts, which says that DVSI's encoder divided the blocks so too. What DVSI's codec holds (a table or a rule) is not known, nor whether every product of DVSI's uses that division. That scratch build was measured on the development, validation, tone and channel vectors before this set was declared, with the scoreboard's own measures too, so none of those partitions is out of sample for the change, and the limits below were set knowing those results; no build of this change was measured on the held-out partition (irstia and mark). The baseline is the head of the branch below, fix/dvsi-low-band (f725a66). The baseline against the change, development vectors (in sample: the row was found on them). The two max 0 checks on P25 say that no P25 decode of the run's speech vectors changes (speech.pcm_changed_vectors, the hashes of the decoded samples; a vector missing from either run counts as changed) and that no P25 encoder row changes (encoder.rows_changed_vectors, the hashes of the bits the IMBE encoder emits; this counter skips a vector whose baseline holds no row hash, so it rests on every speech vector carrying a row hash in both runs, which is to be counted in both reports and stated with the result). They say nothing of inputs outside the run. For D-STAR and rate 33, decoding DVSI's bits: the increase rule asks for a mean gain in waveform correlation with DVSI's decode, sample against sample at lag 0 (vs_dvsi.waveform_corr_unshifted), of at least the stated value with its bootstrap 95% interval (resampling whole recordings) above 0, and all_no_decrease allows no vector's correlation to fall by more than the stated little; the decrease rule asks for a mean fall in log-spectral distance from DVSI's decode (vs_dvsi.lsd_db) with its interval below 0, and all_no_increase bounds any one vector's rise; the envelope correlation with DVSI's decode may fall by no more than the stated little in the mean; the log-spectral distance from the input speech (ours.lsd_db), which no earlier set of this series could ask to fall, is to fall in the mean with its interval below 0, no vector rising by more than the stated little: the change is to bring the decode nearer DVSI's and nearer the input at once; the level against DVSI's decode (vs_dvsi.level_offset_db) may move by no more than the stated mean and worst-vector amounts. The encoder checks compare the two runs' encodings, both decoded by the candidate's decoder: encoder.vs_dvsi_bits.* against DVSI's bits decoded by the same decoder, encoder.lsd_db against the input speech. Here the D-STAR and rate-33 encoders' bits are meant to change (every frame they send at 20 harmonics, and the frames whose prediction it reaches), while P25's must not. The encoder checks judge what the two encodings decode to under one decoder, not what DVSI's decoder would make of them. For the encoders: the distance of our decoded encoding from DVSI's decoded encoding is to fall in the mean with its interval below 0, no vector rising by more than the stated amount; its distance from the input may not rise in the mean; its level against DVSI's decoded encoding may move by no more than the stated mean and worst-vector amounts. What these checks do not establish: that the gain comes from the frames of 20 harmonics alone (the scoreboard's measures are whole-file), the listening quality, or anything of inputs outside the run. Coverage, read on the baseline's own scoreboard of the development, validation, tone and channel partitions (a build of git archive f725a66 scoring itself, aligned freely), compared with itself through the scoreboard's compare() and check_gates() before this set was declared: no check of this set reports missing pairs; every speech measure named is measured on all 20 development vectors in both codecs, the encoder measures on all 20, P25's hashes on all 20.

p25-decoder-development.description: Four rules of DVSI's P25 decoder: this change set is to make the P25 decoder's pitch and P25's subframe rendering (MBE_VOICED_SYNTHESIS_DVSI_IMBE) follow four rules measured on DVSI's decodes of its own P25 encodings. 1. Between two models that both have a voiced band, the mid-frame pitch is the parabola through the square root at 1, 1.5 and 2 of the mantissa y in [1, 2) of the product of the two fundamentals in cycles per sample, floor(2^19 sqrt(fa fb) q(y) / sqrt(y)) / 2^19, in place of the geometric mean; at an onset or an offset the voiced model's own pitch stays. 3. The phase kernel reads a band the model holds as unvoiced with the unvoiced factor taken out, its log2 amplitude plus -log2(0.2046 / sqrt(w0)) (2.289 plus half log2 of w0, the half-rate standard's TIA-102.BABA-1 log-magnitude domain, in which the AMBE codecs' decoded unvoiced amplitudes already are), decided by the decoded voicing, for a frame's own model and through the mid-frame envelope alike. 4. The frame's own models (the last frame's and this one's) are voiced by the 500 Hz columns the mid-frame rule already reads for P25: a harmonic is voiced if the column of its frequency, or of its frequency plus 250 Hz, is, a band that turns taking its magnitude across the unvoiced factor; what the mid-frame rule's first clause (a band in the same state in both frames keeps it) compares once the own models read by columns is to be decided on the development and validation vectors. No constant is fitted for any of the four: the grid is the tone path's, the parabola is the interpolant, 2.289 and one half are the half-rate standard's and the columns are the library's existing ones. Rules 2, 3 and 4 are properties of the rendering: the decoded models, their voicing, amplitudes and prediction history and everything the encoders read stay as decoded (the pitch apart, which rule 1 sets). ProVoice (which has no DVSI material: its nominal pitch and its own rendering stay in all four respects), D-STAR, rate 33, the TIA-102.BABA rendering of mbe_synthesizeSpeechf() and every encoder are to stay byte for byte as they are. How it was found: on DVSI's decodes of the 20 development and 5 validation vectors and of DVSI's synthetic pulse-train vectors, by a scratch build of the library (a worktree at 47d8cf3 with environment switches, outside the repository): the lag of DVSI's decode against ours at frame boundaries and its change over each frame (which the mid-frame pitch alone sets), the per-code drift of the pulse train over runs at one pitch code, the phase of DVSI's voiced harmonics against ours by the frame's voiced share and by the distance to the voicing boundary, and the coherence of DVSI's decode with ours in the band of each unvoiced harmonic; each rule was found only once the one before it was in, and what DVSI's decoder computes is not known beyond its output. That scratch build was measured on the development, validation, tone and channel vectors before these sets were declared, with the scoreboard's own measures too, so none of those partitions is out of sample for the rules, and the limits below were set knowing those results; no build of this change was measured on the held-out partition (irstia and mark). The baseline is the head of the branch below, fix/dvsi-low-band (f725a66). The baseline against the change, development vectors (in sample: the rules were found on them). The max 0 check on speech.pcm_changed_vectors says that no D-STAR or rate-33 decode of the run's speech vectors changes (the decoded PCM's hash, a vector without a hash on either side counting as changed). The max 0 check on encoder.rows_changed_vectors says that no encoder row of the run's speech vectors changes in any mode (the hashes of the bits each encoder emits; this counter skips a vector whose baseline holds no row hash, so 'no encoder row changes' rests on every speech vector carrying a row hash in both runs, which is to be counted in both reports and stated with the result): the encoders' bits must not change at all. Neither says anything of other inputs. For P25 decoding DVSI's bits: the increase rule asks for a mean gain in waveform correlation with DVSI's decode, sample against sample at lag 0 (vs_dvsi.waveform_corr_unshifted), of at least 0.003 with its bootstrap 95% interval (resampling whole recordings) above 0, and all_no_decrease 0 lets no vector's correlation fall at all; the decrease rule asks for a mean fall in log-spectral distance from DVSI's decode (vs_dvsi.lsd_db) of at least 0.06 dB with its interval below 0, and all_no_increase 0 lets no vector's distance from DVSI's decode rise at all; the envelope correlation with DVSI's decode may fall by no more than 0.0002 in the mean; the log-spectral distance from the input speech (ours.lsd_db) may rise by no more than 0.012 dB in the mean and 0.04 dB on any vector, which is the change's cost and is allowed, not hidden: the column reading of rule 4 voices harmonics that the analysis of the input left unvoiced, and a decode that follows DVSI's there moves away from the input; the level against DVSI's decode (vs_dvsi.level_offset_db) may move by no more than 0.03 dB in the mean. Every paired check of P25's decode requires a measurement on every vector of the partition (every_vector), which makes a check need the figure everywhere and does not turn a limit on the mean into one on each vector: the envelope correlation, the level and the no_increase limit on ours.lsd_db bound the mean and no single vector. The two encoder measures (encoder.lsd_db, the IMBE encoder's decoded encoding against the input speech, and encoder.vs_dvsi_bits.lsd_db, against DVSI's decode of DVSI's bits) may rise by no more than 0.01 dB in the mean: both runs' encodings are decoded by the candidate's decoder, so with the encoder's bits unchanged the two are equal by construction, and the checks are there to catch a bit that does change. The measures are the scoreboard's, on the frames it measures; they do not say which of the four rules moved which frames, nor how the change sounds against the input beyond the log-spectral distance. Coverage, read on the baseline's own scoreboard of the development, validation, tone and channel partitions (a build of git archive f725a66 scoring itself, aligned freely, encoders on) before these sets were declared: every paired metric checked here is measured in P25 on all 20 vectors of the partition, and all 20 vectors carry an encoder-row hash and every speech vector a decoded-PCM hash in each of the three modes.
